heroHeadline: Day 668: Extradition Standoff Day 23 — FGR Locates Rocha Moya at Government Palace, Has Not Summoned Him; Seven of Ten Indicted Officials Remain in Mexico
heroSubtitle: 668 days of cartel civil war — May 22: The US-Mexico extradition standoff enters Day 23 with no resolution. Mexican federal prosecutors (FGR) have reportedly identified Rocha Moya's location — believed to be inside Culiacán's Government Palace under aerial drone surveillance — yet have not formally summoned the indicted governor to testify. Three of ten SDNY-indicted officials are in US federal custody at Brooklyn MDC (Mérida Sánchez, Díaz Vega, Inzunza Cazárez); seven including Rocha Moya and Mayor Gámez Mendívil remain in Mexico as FGR reviews US extradition documentation under the 60-day treaty clock (Article 11, Mexico-US extradition treaty). UIF has frozen Rocha Moya's domestic bank accounts (May 15). President Sheinbaum maintains 'not a protectorate' sovereignty posture citing the US rejection of 36 Mexican extradition requests. El Mayo Zambada's EDNY sentencing — scheduled May 18, postponed a 3rd time — now targets July 20 before Judge Brian Cogan; defense memo due July 6. Ovidio sentencing (NDIL, Chicago) set for July 27. May 20 OFAC crypto sanctions (11 Chapitos launderers, 6 Ethereum wallets) continue reverberating through global cryptocurrency exchanges. La Mayiza ~90% territorial control; 13,300+ federal troops deployed under interim Governor Bonilla Valverde. Running conflict toll: ~2,425+ homicides (Noroeste) / 3,000+ (WSJ) since September 9, 2024; ~5,800 disappearances (NGO Sabuesos Unidas AC).
